entries.root_cause: Job-level explicit YAML keys had been fail-closed, but step parsing still attempted to interpret explicit mapping syntax and therefore accepted a folded block-scalar key whose semantic value was `if`. A required governance step could be skipped while the authority validator remained green.

Supersession validation proved target existence and acyclicity but did not enforce the register's append-only replacement rule. An accepted decision could point backward to an older unrelated ID and falsely present it as the successor without appending a new replacement decision.

The project-memory workflow validator proved the existence of named exact-head steps but did not bind the complete step sequence or forbid an additional checkout after HEAD verification. A later checkout could replace the verified worktree with accepted main before all governance checks executed.

Decision immutability was anchored only to the original seeded IDs 001-017. A decision appended by a later accepted change was therefore not automatically promoted into the immutable historical baseline and could be deleted or have its proposition rewritten by a future PR.

Decision discovery treated any visible row beginning with a canonical decision ID as a definition without validating the complete four-column record. A truncated appended row could therefore satisfy supersession target existence while carrying no proposition, status or accepted authority/source.
